description: Reasoning vault for solving trigonometric equations, aligned with OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e Section 9.5 (fundamental identities, quadratic-in-form equations, multiple-angle equations, squaring with extraneous-root checking, and periodic applications).

archetypes.name: Rewriting Mixed-Function Trigonometric Equations via Identities (Find-the-Flaw)
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §9.5 — Solving Trigonometric Equations Using Fundamental Identities & Quadratic in Form
archetypes.coreConcept: To solve an equation mixing trigonometric functions or double angles (such as cos(2x) with sin x, or sin^2 x with cos x), substitute a fundamental Pythagorean or double-angle identity so the expression depends on a single trigonometric function in quadratic form before factoring. L3 problem form: show a worked solution that makes a listed identity or sign mistake; the prompt shows the work as 'Line N: $...$' lines and the learner picks the first wrong line (answerSpec choice with verify.flaw; asking for the simplified expression lets the learner just recompute, 06 §2.3).
archetypes.mentalModel: Translating a multi-function trigonometric expression into a single-variable quadratic without breaking algebraic equivalence.

archetypes.name: Solving Quadratic-Form & Identity Trigonometric Equations on [0, 2pi)
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §9.5 — Solving Trigonometric Equations That Are Quadratic in Form, Using Fundamental Identities, and Multiple Angles
archetypes.coreConcept: Choose an appropriate Pythagorean or double-angle identity to convert a trigonometric equation into a single function, solve the resulting quadratic by factoring, discard any trigonometric ratio outside [-1, 1] (or outside the function's domain), and find every exact solution in [0, 2pi) using reference angles and quadrant signs.
archetypes.mentalModel: Projecting valid algebraic factor roots onto the unit circle to collect every quadrant solution within one full 2pi interval.

archetypes.name: Coupled Trigonometric Modeling via Squaring and Extraneous-Root Filtering
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §9.5 — Solving Trigonometric Equations Using Fundamental Identities (with squaring and extraneous-solution checking)
archetypes.coreConcept: When combining two geometric, vector, or waveform relations produces an equation linking distinct trigonometric functions linearly (such as a*sin(theta) + b*cos(theta) = c), isolate or rearrange terms, square both sides, apply a Pythagorean identity to find candidate angles, and substitute every candidate back into the original unsquared equation to discard extraneous solutions introduced by squaring.
archetypes.mentalModel: Squaring expands the solution set by erasing relative signs; only candidates that survive substitution into the original signed equation are valid.
archetypes.governingRelation: A(\theta) = B(\theta) \implies A(\theta)^2 = B(\theta)^2,\quad \text{verify } A(\theta_k) = B(\theta_k)

archetypes.name: Periodic Sinusoidal Modeling and Threshold-Crossing Duration
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §9.5 — Solving Trigonometric Equations with Multiple Angles & Real-World Applications
archetypes.coreConcept: Construct a sinusoidal model y(t) = A*trig(2*pi*t/T) + D from physical bounds (minimum, maximum, period T, and initial state at t = 0), combine it with a threshold or clearance target y(t) = y_target, solve the resulting multiple-angle trigonometric equation over one cycle, and verify which sub-interval satisfies the directional inequality (above vs below threshold) to find the crossing time or active duration.
archetypes.mentalModel: Translating cyclic bounds into a sinusoidal curve, intersecting it with a threshold level, and identifying the active phase interval within one period.
archetypes.governingRelation: y(t) = D \pm A\cos\!\left(\frac{2\pi}{T}t\right),\quad A = \frac{y_{\max} - y_{\min}}{2},\quad D = \frac{y_{\max} + y_{\min}}{2}
